newsitem.title: UK: New sugar freight business sighted but rates weak.
newsitem.headline: New sugar freight business sighted but rates weak.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a series of fresh orders on Wednesday although rates for some key routes appeared to be slipping, shipbrokers said.

CSR was said to be closely working its recent order for 6,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Prai for 5/15 November at between $16.75 and $17.00, under the rate achieved for the last similar fixture.
Shipbrokers said CSR fixed 20,000 tonnes, again in bulk, Queensland to Japan for 1/10 November at around $17.00, adding that although the size was larger, the rate still seemed low.
"That's also relatively cheap, or slightly softer," the shipbroker said. "Rates seem to be weakening in the Pacific."
Benham was reported to be on subjects with 18,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio or Recife to Toronto for end October.

New business included orders from the South Africa Sugar Association, which quoted for around 18,000 tonnes in bulk from Durban to US Gulf/Atlantic for 24/31 October and Genoc with 18,250 tonnes from Maputo to Leixoes for early November.
Czarnikow Rionda was open with new enquiries for bulk sugar cargoes.
It quoted for 14/17,000 tonnes from Rosario to US Gulf/Atlantic for end October/early November and 12/13,650 tonnes from Buenaventura to Sri Lanka for 5/15 November.
